bullets.title: Fed hikes 25bp as expected; hawkish dots signal more tightening ahead
bullets.body: The Fed raised rates 25bp to 3.75-4.00% in a unanimous decision. Chair Warsh signaled inflation is the predominant focus with financial conditions 'not restrictive'—16 of 18 officials project at least one more 2026 hike. The neutral rate dot moved up to 3.25%, the highest since 2016, and 2027 dots showed no cuts. Goldman Sachs now expects an October hike (58% probability per prediction markets, ~84% per some surveys); Morgan Stanley projects December and March hikes to terminal 4.25-4.50%.

bullets.title: Market breadth deteriorating sharply; >50% of S&P stocks below 200-DMA
bullets.body: Over 50% of S&P 500 constituents are trading below their 200-day moving average, the weakest breadth since early April. A technical analyst notes S&P is knocking on new highs while more stocks sit at lows than highs—historical analogs only in January 1973 and November 1999. Goldman's panic index saw its third-largest single-day decline in history on Thursday, suggesting some tactical relief, while CTAs are positioned as sellers in all scenarios next week.

bullets.title: US 10-year yield breaks 5% for first time since 2007; 2-year at 4.76%
bullets.body: The 10-year Treasury yield briefly pierced 5% this week—its highest since 2007—driven by oil-driven inflation shock and the hawkish Fed. The 2-year hit 4.76%, highest since July 2024. Hedgeye's models project 2-year and 10-year cycle highs at 4.85% and 5.12% respectively. JPMorgan raised its year-end 2026 2-year and 10-year forecasts by 40bp and 20bp to 4.70% and 5.05%.

bullets.title: G7 sovereign borrowing costs hit post-2008 highs; France downgraded to A+
bullets.body: Average G7 country borrowing costs reached their highest level since 2008. France's 10-year yield hit 4.56%—a 16-year high—and the French-German spread widened to 100bp for the first time since 2012. Scope rating agency downgraded France to A+ from AA-. France's public debt-to-GDP is projected at 119.3% in 2026 and 121.7% in 2027.

bullets.title: AI safety/pacing debate roils semis -6% vs software +5% in record divergence
bullets.body: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for slowing frontier AI model development, triggering a record single-session spread: SOX fell 5.9% while software (IGV) gained 5% (+12.5pp spread, a 2.5 sigma event). NVDA, AVGO, MRVL, and ORCL all fell 3-9%. However, both NVDA CEO Jensen Huang and Broadcom CEO Hock Tan dismissed the slowdown narrative and reaffirmed capex targets—AVGO reiterated its $115B FY2027 AI semiconductor revenue forecast. Trump also publicly rejected calls to slow AI development.

bullets.title: Big Tech uses ~$300B in off-balance-sheet guarantees to obscure AI capex exposure
bullets.body: The FT reports that large technology companies are using guarantee structures to keep approximately $300 billion in AI infrastructure commitments off their balance sheets, avoiding recognition in financial statements. Goldman Sachs forecasts $420B in hyperscaler gross debt issuance in 2027—a 60%+ increase from an estimated $250B in 2026—as capex continues to escalate. Hyperscalers are projected to spend $784B in capex in 2026.

bullets.title: US industrial production flat in August; manufacturing -0.3% vs +0.3% consensus
bullets.body: August industrial production was flat m/m vs. +0.3% consensus, with manufacturing declining 0.3% against the +0.3% forecast. Capacity utilization came in at 76.3%, a touch below the 76.4% estimate. All three key data releases on September 18 missed expectations. Morgan Stanley raised Q3 GDP tracking to 2.4% on strong retail sales earlier in the week.

bullets.title: Oil above $100/bbl as Saudi East-West pipeline offline; diesel at record $6.45/gallon
bullets.body: WTI crude rose above $103-106/bbl as Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline was taken offline by Houthi drone strikes (repair expected to take 3-5 weeks), Red Sea traffic collapsed to 4 vessels/day vs. a 16/day 10-day average, and Aramco cut European crude allocations to zero for next month. US diesel hit a record $6.45/gallon (AAA), up 68% year-over-year. US gas prices averaged $4.43/gallon, the highest September level on record. JPMorgan estimates ~$16 geopolitical risk premium embedded in Brent crude.

bullets.title: Trump announces 'AI Force' and AI czar; opposes frontier model development slowdown
bullets.body: President Trump announced the creation of an 'AI Force' modeled on the Space Force and plans to name an AI czar soon. Trump publicly rejected Anthropic's call for a frontier AI development slowdown, calling AI America's 'next Industrial Revolution.' Trump projects AI could reach 25% of US GDP and says the US will not allow a slowdown that would cede leadership to China.

bullets.title: Bessent-He Lifeng talks at JPMorgan HQ ahead of Trump-Xi summit September 24
bullets.body: US Treasury Secretary Bessent met China's Vice Premier He Lifeng at JPMorgan HQ in New York to set the stage for the Trump-Xi summit. Discussions included AI governance and guardrails for autonomous weapons, rare earths, agricultural purchases, and extension of the Busan trade truce. A senior US official confirmed AI risks and safeguards are formally on the bilateral agenda. The yuan midpoint strengthened to its best level since February 2023.

bullets.title: BoJ raises rates to 1.25%, 31-year high, but yen weakens on dovish dissents
bullets.body: The Bank of Japan raised its overnight call rate by 25bp to 1.25% in a 7-2 vote, sending it to its highest level since 1995. Two dissenting votes and Governor Ueda's dovish press conference—stressing gradualism and uncertainty on the terminal rate—caused the yen to weaken rather than strengthen, with USDJPY breaking above 157. Citigroup revised its BoJ rate path to hikes in December 2026, March, and July 2027.

bullets.title: BoE holds at 3.75% but signals November hike; launches multi-year QT guidance
bullets.body: The Bank of England held rates at 3.75% in a 6-3 vote but signaled a near-term hike is likely as inflation accelerated to 3.1% year-over-year in August and services inflation remains sticky at 3.4%. JPMorgan and other banks now expect a November hike and February 2027 hike. The BoE also announced a multi-year QT framework: £20B per year in active Gilt sales to HM Treasury through 2034, averaging ~£46B annually.

bullets.title: Goldman warns CTAs are sellers in all scenarios next week; Panic Index third-largest decline
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs reports its Panic Index saw its third-largest single-day decline in history on Thursday, suggesting positions were cleaner. However, the Goldman flows team warns that CTAs are positioned as sellers across all equity scenarios heading into next week. The bank's macro traders describe positioning as 'cleaner after a deleveraging event.'

bullets.title: Meta Muse launches at #1 on App Store; META adds 90-day upside catalyst watch
bullets.body: Meta's Muse AI agent hit the #1 spot on the US Apple App Store free apps, surpassing ChatGPT. The app achieved 900K+ downloads in its first week. Citi and others added 90-day positive catalyst watches ahead of Meta Connect September 23-24. Meta also launched the tiered Meta One subscription service (starting at $2.99/month) and announced in-house Arke chip deployment in H1 2027. Morgan Stanley sees a $30 trillion consumer spending TAM addressable by agentic commerce, with META among the best-positioned.

bullets.title: NVDA CEO expects chip sales to double next year; GPU cloud prices up 17-21%
bullets.body: NVDA CEO Jensen Huang said at the All-In Summit that the company expects to sell twice as many chips next year driven by broad AI adoption. GPU cloud providers including Nebius raised on-demand instance prices 17-21% effective October 1 (H100 to $4.50/hr, B200 to $8.50/hr), signaling supply/demand tightness. CoreWeave upsized its convertible note offering from $3B to $3.7B. Huang also noted that AI safety monitoring requires ~20% of inference compute overhead.

bullets.title: Memory supercycle thesis building: DRAM ASPs +20-30% QoQ in 3Q; HBM tight through 2030
bullets.body: BofA's Simon Woo reports 3Q DRAM ASPs rose 20-30% QoQ despite rising LTA mix. Intel CEO warned memory prices have jumped 5-7x with memory now comprising ~75% of cost for lower-end phones and laptops. NVDA CFO described memory prices as 'extreme' and expects pricing pressure to extend through 2028, compressing near-term margins to 71-72%. SK Hynix does not expect HBM supply-demand balance until 2030. Micron demonstrated the world's first 512GB DDR5 module with volume production targeted for H2 2027.

bullets.title: US housing market: record 563K seller-buyer gap; starts miss badly; NAHB hits 2-year low
bullets.body: US home sellers outnumber buyers by a record 563,000 (58% gap), per Redfin—the largest since 2013. August housing starts fell 2.6% m/m vs. +6.7% forecast; multifamily starts collapsed 21.7% m/m. The NAHB index fell to 32 in September, its lowest in a year. The 30-year mortgage rate is running at 6.97-7.24%.

bullets.title: US wage inflation reaccelerating; initial claims at sub-200K for first time since mid-July
bullets.body: Initial jobless claims fell to 196K in the latest reading, the first sub-200K print since mid-July and near multi-decade lows. Continuing claims hit 1.73M, the lowest since early 2024. Hedgeye's macro model shows multiple indicators of wage inflation reacceleration including rising regional survey wage components and small business hiring plans near cycle highs. The Atlanta Fed GDP Now also moved to ~5% for Q3.

bullets.title: ECB signals additional tightening; hawkish shift across developed-market central banks
bullets.body: ECB member Stournaras opened the door to an October rate hike if inflation rises, while the ECB's Lagarde acknowledged rising energy prices and upside inflation risks. JPMorgan now expects an additional ECB hike in March 2027 (raising their forecast from a prior hold), bringing the deposit rate to 3%. This marks the first month in decades where the Fed, BoJ, BoE, and ECB are all tightening simultaneously. France's 10Y OAT yield spread over Bunds widened to 100bp.

bullets.title: Geopolitical risk elevated: Strait of Hormuz, Iran/Saudi escalation, North Korea missiles
bullets.body: Iran's Strait of Hormuz closure continued, with commodity vessel traffic at just 4 ships/day vs. a 16/day 10-day average. CENTCOM reported 1B barrels of crude safely transited since operations began. Iran's Parliament Speaker stated the strait would not reopen until 'all conditions are met.' Houthis struck an Aramco facility in Yanbu, triggering air alerts in Riyadh. North Korea fired a second ballistic missile into the Sea of Japan. Trump described major Iranian action as pending, saying 'very big things' are coming.
